_comment: One of the nine plain colours, and it sets every colour knob it can reach -- the vault, the air, the
cloud, the star this world goes round and the curtain that stands over its cold. It declares no
aspects: `Word.aspects` is widened from the parameters a word sets, so the `sets` map is the whole of
the declaration and attachment does the rest. `red sky` paints the vault, `red sun` the star, `red and
green aurora` the ramp from its crown to its hem, and `a red Age` means all of them at once.
The light is deliberately *not* among them. Saying the light here is red is a different claim from
saying the sky is, and `witchlight` is the idiom that already makes it.
These replaced `crimson`, `emerald` and `violet`, and retired `verdigris` -- which was `sky: green` and
nothing else, which is `green sky` said in a word a writer has to learn first (Jonah, 2026-08-29).
